description: Two side-by-side bright-field TEM micrographs of the same region of deformed Fe–28% Al, imaged under opposite diffraction conditions (the images themselves carry no +g / −g label; the caption states the pair is +g and −g with g = ±2 0 0 near a [0 0 1] zone axis). Both panels show a heavily dislocated substructure of dark, largely straight dislocation lines with some curved segments crossing a light matrix, plus dark dot-like clusters and faint bend-contour / thickness contrast. A black arrow near the lower edge of each panel marks the imaging g vector (up-left in the left panel, down-right in the right panel); a 0.2 µm scale bar is printed at the lower right of the left panel. The right-hand panel carries annotation: closely spaced parallel dislocation pairs labelled "d" (dipole pairs, identified because their relative positions reverse when the sign of g is changed) and further paired dislocations labelled "p" (pairs sharing identical Burgers vectors, i.e. non-dipole pairs). The figure demonstrates that the near-screw superdislocations in deformed Fe–28% Al are arranged either as dipoles or as identical-Burgers-vector dislocation pairs.

observations.observation: The group is a pair of bright-field TEM micrographs showing dark dislocation lines and networks in the matrix of deformed Fe–28% Al.
A scale bar in the lower right of the left panel is printed as 0.2 µm.
Each panel contains a single black arrow indicating the imaging g vector; no crystallographic indices are printed next to the arrows.
The right panel is annotated with 'd' (dipole pairs) and 'p' (non-dipole/identical-Burgers-vector pairs), whereas the left panel carries no such letter labels.

The caption states the pair of micrographs is taken in +g and −g imaging conditions, with zone axis near [0 0 1] and imaging g vector (arrowed) of ±2 0 0; the images themselves do not state which panel is +g and which is −g.
The caption states that dipole pairs (marked d) are confirmed by the change of relative dislocation position when the sign of the imaging vector is reversed.
The sample the figure is about is deformed Fe–28% Al, per the caption.

The citing text states that many of the uniformly distributed superdislocations examined in +g and −g conditions are arranged in dipole configurations (marked d), while other pairs have identical Burgers vectors (marked p).
The citing text states that the dislocations in these micrographs are generally straight and mostly in near-screw orientations along {1 1 0} glide planes.

The citing text states that reactions between superdislocations with different <1 1 1> Burgers vectors lying in different {1 1 0} planes produce sessile [1 0 0] edge-dislocation pairs on a cube plane, forming locks that prevent further room-temperature superdislocation motion.
Dark dot-like clusters and speckled background contrast are scattered across both micrographs; their nature is not resolvable at this magnification.
Dislocation line lengths are not quantified and no numeric density or Burgers-vector value is printed anywhere in the figure; only the 0.2 µm scale bar provides a length reference.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–28% Al (unlabelled as to +g/−g). Heavy, mostly straight dislocation lines forming networks; dark dot-like clusters. A black arrow at the lower edge indicates the imaging g vector, and a white-boxed scale bar reads 0.2 µm.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the same/allied area under the opposite imaging condition. Parallel dislocation pairs are annotated: 'd' for dipole pairs and 'p' for pairs with identical Burgers vectors; a black arrow at the lower-right marks the g vector. No scale bar is printed in this panel.
